Code **d** means "Poor (use with caution)". It is the lowest reliability grade CMHC publishes. For averages such as average rent, it applies when the coefficient of variation (CV) is above 7.5% and up to 10%. For vacancy rates, the code is set from the CV together with the rate, the sampling fraction and the universe size. Estimates with a CV over 10% are suppressed and shown as "**".

CMHC releases an estimate only if it rests on **4 or more responding entities**. This is a confidentiality rule. Unit counts are the exception, since they are counts and not estimates.

I took both points from the CMHC Rental Market Survey methodology (published 2024-01-29), as summarised in this server's docs://cmhc/rms-methodology page. I did not open CMHC's own page. Some CMHC tables label code d "Fair" instead of "Poor", so check the wording on the table you're using.
